newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Rugby Union-Miller to face former Leinster allies.
newsitem.headline: Rugby Union-Miller to face former Leinster allies.

text.p: Former Ireland "A' international Eric Miller said he would not let sentiment get in his way when he lined out for English club side Leicester against Leinster in a European Cup Pool B match at Lansdowne Road on Wednesday.
"I know a lot of the Leinster players since I played for the province myself but all friendships will be put aside until after the match," the number eight said.
"Sentiment will not get in the way," he added.
Leinster have made two changes to the side defeated 34-17 by Welsh side Llanelli in their opening Pool B outing for this evening's home fixture (kick-off at 1745 GMT).
Alan McGowan returns at fly-half for Leinster in place of Richard Governey and Martin Ridge, fit again after a shoulder injury, takes over from Ray McIreavy in the centre.
The home side had to plan without promising winger Denis Hickie and back row forward Dean Oswald.
Leicester will be without England number eight Dean Richards and winger Rory Underwood but they will have international second-row Martin Johnson in their side.

Because of injuries to key players, Irish provincial champions Munster had to wait until Tuesday evening before they finalised their team to meet Cardiff in a Pool D game at the Arms Park in Wales (kick-off 1815 GMT).

Munster made two changes, both at prop forward, to the side that beat Milan 23-5 on Saturday with Ian Murray coming in at loose-head for John Fitzgerald and Noel Healy at tight-head for Paul McCarthy.
Cardiff, who lost to Toulouse after extra-time in the 1995 European Cup final, beat England's Wasps with a late drop-goal by Jonathan Davies in their opening round game last Sunday.
They have made just one change, Mark Bennett coming in at flank-forward for Jamie Ringer.

Ulster, who have already had to plan without the services of backs Mark McCall and Maurice Field, will give centre Sheldon Coulter a late fitness test ahead of their meeting with Harlequins at Ravenhill in Belfast (kick-off 1800 GMT).

Sheldon received a knock to the face in the 41-34 defeat of Scotland's Catelonia on Sunday but he is expected to be passed fit to play as is Ireland international second-row Jeremy Davidson who is under treatment for a toe injury.
Harlequins will have Ireland international Jim Staples at full-back, former England captain Will Carling at fly-half and two rugby league stars, Gary Connolly and Robbie Paul, in the centres.
Connacht, who defeated Padova 34-12 in Galway on Saturday will travel to meet Welsh side Dunvant in a European Conference game (kick-off at 1815 GMT).
